title: Chapter 76
content:
The sports car obliterated the front entrance with a concussive roar, sending splintered timber and plaster raining across the hood and windshield.

Twin halogen beams pierced the dust-choked gloom of the cottage. Gazing through the cracked glass, Il-hyun’s brow furrowed into a sharp, displeased scowl.

Beside him, Jakyeong wore an identical look of utter bewilderment.

Standing in the center of the ruined living room was a lone figure. Even silhouetted in the headlights, the posture was undeniably that of someone who hadn't come armed for a hit.

Il-hyun rolled down his window as the figure marched toward the driver's side on furious, clicking heels.

"Are you completely out of your mind?! Were you trying to run me down?!"

Recognizing the sharp, indignant voice, Il-hyun cursed under his breath and pushed the door open. He flicked the main light switches, flooding the wreckage with warm light to properly reveal the trespasser.

Kang Yu-jung.

Standing in stylish resort casuals, Il-hyun's older sister was glaring daggers at him with hands planted on her hips.

"What on earth are you doing here?" Il-hyun asked, entirely unbothered by the destruction.

"I heard you took off on unannounced leave, so I came looking for you," she snapped. "Chief Park wouldn't give me a straight answer, which meant you were hiding out down here."

"I asked why."

"Are you playing dumb? Tomorrow is your birthday."

Glancing over her shoulder, a boutique pastry box and several luxury gift bags sat neatly arranged on the dining table. Il-hyun clicked his tongue in mild annoyance.

"If you let yourself in, you could have at least turned on a lamp. Why were you lurking in the dark like a sewer rat?"

"You ungrateful little brat! Calling your own sister a rat? I was trying to surprise you! How was I supposed to know you'd drive a sports car through the front porch?! You nearly turned your birthday into my memorial service!"

Fuming, Yu-jung’s eyes drifted toward the passenger side, freezing the moment they locked onto the young man stepping out of the vehicle.

Jakyeong stood frozen in the headlights, caught off guard and entirely unsure of how to navigate the sudden family reunion.

Yu-jung’s gaze shifted back and forth between her brother and the boy, her eyes widening in disbelief.

Il-hyun crooked a finger, beckoning Jakyeong over. As Jakyeong reluctantly stepped into the light, Yu-jung’s jaw dropped.

"Yi-an...?"

"H-Hello, ma'am," Jakyeong stammered awkwardly.

"How... how are you here?"

Il-hyun made the introductions with deadpan indifference. "You met him last year, so you know the face. This is my older sister, Kang Yu-jung."

His dark eyes drifted from his sister back to Jakyeong. The sharp, dismissive edge in his expression instantly melted away, replaced by an affectionate warmth and a subtle, teasing smirk.

"And this is Lee Ja-kyeong."

Yu-jung tilted her head, clearly puzzled. Not Jang Yi-an? Lee Ja-kyeong?

Before she could voice the question, Il-hyun delivered the coup de grâce with radiant, unabashed pride:

"My lover."

Both Yu-jung and Jakyeong’s jaws hit the floor in unison.

"What?!"

"That is not true!" Jakyeong barked in frantic denial.

Il-hyun merely offered an indulgent, knowing grin. "As you can see, our darling is dreadfully shy."

Jakyeong bristled, his face flushing with mortification. "Please don't misunderstand! President Kang is making a terrible joke!"

Utterly lost, Yu-jung blinked, looking between the two men with round, astonished eyes.

Even amidst the chaos, Jakyeong couldn't help privately admiring her. A year had passed, yet Kang Yu-jung remained breathtakingly striking—effortlessly elegant and radiating an intoxicating, mature grace.

Caught in his brief trance, Jakyeong barely registered Il-hyun’s reaction until a large, heavy palm clamped directly over his eyes, shoving him backward by the forehead.

"Introductions over. Go to your room."

Go to my room? After you turned the living room into an open-air parking lot?

Looking around, the structural beams were groaning, though the rest of the cottage seemed miraculously stable. Resisting the hold was useless; Il-hyun firmly marched him down the hall, practically shoving him through the bedroom door and clicking the latch shut.

Does Kang Yu-jung know nothing about the syndicate war?

Jakyeong pressed his ear to the wood, but the conversation down the hall was muffled beneath the hum of the sea breeze.

Turning around with a tired sigh, he caught sight of the life-sized silicone replica standing by the window. Even veiled beneath a linen sheet with only the feet exposed, the uncanny clone sent a cold prickle down his neck.

Sitting on the edge of the mattress, he turned Yu-jung’s words over in his head.

Tomorrow is his birthday.

Why hadn't the man mentioned it? Given Kang Il-hyun’s greedy, exploitative nature, he usually weaponized every petty excuse under the sun to extort concessions and favors.

With the conversation outside dragging on, Jakyeong stepped into the bathroom to wash away the salt spray. He smoked a cigarette, took a hot shower, and threw on a fresh shirt and sweatpants.

While drying his hair, the low rumble of a vehicle echoed from the gravel drive outside.

As he stepped toward the door, a knock sounded, and Il-hyun strolled inside with a lit cigarette between his lips and a white bakery box in hand.

Catching sight of the draped mannequin in the corner, Il-hyun walked over and whipped the linen sheet off in one fluid motion.

The uncannily accurate silicone clone stood bare in the dim light. Il-hyun scanned the figure from head to toe, looking thoroughly satisfied with his commission.

"Truly an immaculate piece of work."

Setting the cake on the nightstand, Il-hyun spun the mannequin around, casually tugging its waistband down. The permanent tattoo branded over the right hip and the subtle dimple in the lower back were replicated in precise detail. Il-hyun traced the ink with his thumb, then gave the silicone cheek a firm, approving squeeze.

Jakyeong watched with visceral disgust. "Stop groping a doll and get away from it."

Il-hyun turned around, a look of theatrical regret crossing his handsome features. "I really should have had your actual eyeballs preserved and mounted in its sockets."

Pinching the cigarette between his fingers, Il-hyun pointed the glowing ember directly at Jakyeong’s face. He wore a pleasant smile, but the darkness in his irises burned with lethal, unblinking intensity.

"Consider this your only warning. Look at anyone other than me with those hungry eyes again, and I won't let it slide."

"..."

He noticed.

Jakyeong had only stared at Yu-jung for two seconds in mild admiration. It was pure male instinct to appreciate a gorgeous woman, but arguing the point felt like an express ticket to having his eyeballs gouged out on the spot.

Jakyeong clicked his tongue internally. Given that the man was this territorial toward his own flesh-and-blood sister, decapitating Choi Ki-tae had clearly been an act of calculated routine rather than a sudden fit of rage.

"Did your sister... head back?"

"She left. The resort general manager came by to escort her."

"General manager?"

"Haewon owns the resort on the cape."

No wonder the staff everywhere were bowing like servants. Jakyeong mentally groaned. If the conglomerate owned the five-star luxury resort, why on earth were they roughing it in a battered timber cabin? And now the entire front facade was smashed to pieces.

Il-hyun placed the cake on the table, grinding his cigarette out in the crystal tray.

"Is tomorrow... really your birthday?"

"Yes."

"You should have mentioned it earlier."

Il-hyun arched a brow. "Why? Were you planning on buying me a present?"

Jakyeong kept his mouth shut. Offering gifts to this lunatic was an invitation for depraved, unreasonable demands. Still, had he known in advance, he would have picked up a small token—if only out of professional courtesy to his primary employer.

Il-hyun crossed the room, sinking onto the edge of the mattress beside him. He let out a long, melancholic sigh before resting his head against Jakyeong’s shoulder.

Every time the man pulled this routine, an icy dread gripped Jakyeong's gut.

Il-hyun rubbed his cheek against the cotton of Jakyeong’s shirt, his voice dropping into a soft, sorrowful murmur.

"I’ve never been fond of birthdays, truth be told. It only reminds me of a miserable childhood starved of maternal warmth."

"..."

"Sometimes... I feel as though I should never have been born at all."

Jakyeong shrank back slightly. Despite the tragic cadence, hot lips brushed against his jawline, trailing a slow, wet lick up his cheek before Il-hyun leaned back with a faint, bittersweet smile.

Just as Jakyeong began to lower his guard, Il-hyun delivered the punchline:

"I'm heading in to shower. Then we're having a birthday party."

"A party...?"

"You can celebrate the miracle of my birth with your entire body, darling."

Every other syllable faded, leaving only the words entire body echoing ominously in Jakyeong’s ears. He swallowed a lump of dry nervousness.

Il-hyun flashed a tender, wistful smile and disappeared into the en-suite bath, leaving Jakyeong staring at the white cake box with the stunned expression of a man who had just been blind-sided by a truck.

Fuck. I walked right into his trap.

His tailbone was still throbbing from last night. Surely he wouldn't... not after crashing a car through the living room...

Desperate to avoid another round, Jakyeong pulled the duvet over his head, pretending to be dead to the world. But instead of sleep, his senses remained hyper-alert, tracking every splash of water from the bathroom.

The shower cut off, followed by the heavy click of the door. Jakyeong squeezed his eyes shut.

A firm tug yanked the duvet from the foot of the bed. Jakyeong held on with all his might, but the blanket was stripped away effortlessly. Bolting upright with a glare, he found Kang Il-hyun standing over him in a loose robe, wearing a deeply wounded pout.

"Exhausted already? On my birthday?"

Jakyeong gritted his teeth. You said out of your own mouth you despised birthdays ten minutes ago.

Checking the digital clock, midnight had already passed. He tried to suggest calling it a night, but Il-hyun was entirely unyielding.

Realizing there was no escape, Jakyeong dragged himself over to the table and slid the cake from the box.

The cake was a pristine, snowy mountain of fresh whipped cream.

As Jakyeong reached for the candles, Il-hyun scooped a generous dollop of cream with his index finger, sliding it past his lips with an audible suck before licking the digit clean. His dark eyes took on a slick, hungry sheen—the look of a predator ready to tear into a feast.

He dipped his finger into the cream once more, extending it toward Jakyeong’s mouth.

"Care for a taste, darling?"

"I'll... cut a slice for myself later."

Jakyeong tried to lean back, but Il-hyun rose from his chair and untied the sash of his robe.

The heavy fabric parted, exposing his thick, fully engorged erection standing rigid at full mast.

Here we go again. This unhinged, perverted bastard.

Jakyeong’s face twisted in open, unvarnished revulsion. He briefly debated demanding a toxicology screen; there was no physiological explanation for a man to be standing at full attention twenty-four hours a day without pharmaceutical intervention.

Before a single candle could be lit, Il-hyun leaned over the table and shoved his hard cock straight into the center of the birthday cake.

Jakyeong froze in pure, paralyzed shock.

Il-hyun withdrew with a wet squelch, his shaft entirely coated in thick, white whipped cream.

Jakyeong briefly contemplated taking the lighter and setting the man's cock on fire, but decided his life was worth more than a petty act of arson.

His worst fears were materializing with horrifying speed.

"Since it's my birthday," Il-hyun purred, his voice dropping into a dark, velvet register, "surely I'm entitled to a gift?"

Jakyeong glared up through his dark lashes, silent and defensive.

"I'll be generous... and accept only one present tonight."

The implication was crystal clear: take care of it with his mouth, and his bruised lower half would be spared.

Jakyeong weighed the scales for a brief, calculated moment.

Fine. It's his birthday. He wired an astronomical retainer, and when he caught me escaping, he didn't put a bullet through my skull.

The man was a pathological liar who shamelessly weaponized his dead mother for sympathy, but every time Il-hyun spoke of his miserable childhood, an unwanted echo of Jakyeong’s own past stirred in his chest.

He couldn't fully explain the impulse. Both of them were fundamentally lonely, broken creatures—and on the hierarchy of misery, Il-hyun had likely had it better. At the very least, the billionaire heir had never had to chew on cardboard boxes to stave off starvation as a ten-year-old street urchin.

Yet despite everything, a quiet, irrational part of him wanted to offer that neglected child a shred of comfort.

Jakyeong slid off his chair, sinking onto his knees on the hardwood before Il-hyun.

He parted his lips. Il-hyun guided the cream-slicked head against his mouth.

Jakyeong extended his tongue, tentatively licking the sweet frosting from the warm slit. It tasted remarkably rich and sugary.

Lifting his gaze, his dark irises locked with Kang Il-hyun’s heavy, unblinking stare—a gaze burning with raw, suffocating hunger.
